# vergen/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)// Copyright (c) 2022 vergen developers
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//
[3](https://docs.rs#3)// Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0
[4](https://docs.rs#4)// <LICENSE-APACHE or https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0> or the MIT
[5](https://docs.rs#5)// license <LICENSE-MIT or https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT>, at your
[6](https://docs.rs#6)// option. All files in the project carrying such notice may not be copied,
[7](https://docs.rs#7)// modified, or distributed except according to those terms.
[8](https://docs.rs#8)
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! # vergen - Emit cargo instructions from a build script
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! `vergen`, when used in conjunction with cargo [build scripts] can emit the following:
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//!
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! - Will emit [`cargo:rustc-env=VAR=VALUE`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html#cargorustc-envvarvalue)
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//!   for each feature you have enabled.  These can be referenced with the [`env`!](std::env!) or [`option_env`!](std::option_env!) macro in your code.
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! - Can emit [`cargo:warning`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html#cargo-warning) outputs if the
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//!   [`fail_on_error`](Emitter::fail_on_error) feature is not enabled and the requested variable is defaulted through error or
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//!   the [`idempotent`](Emitter::idempotent) flag.
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! - Will emit [`cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html#rerun-if-changed)
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//!   to rerun instruction emission if the `build.rs` file changed.
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! - Will emit [`cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html#rerun-if-changed)
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//!   to rerun instruction emission if the `VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT` environment variable has changed.
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! - Will emit [`cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=VERGEN_DEFAULT_ON_ERROR`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html#rerun-if-changed)
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//!   to rerun instruction emission if the `VERGEN_DEFAULT_ON_ERROR` environment variable has changed.
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! - Will emit [`cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html#rerun-if-changed)
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//!   to rerun instruction emission if the `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` environment variable has changed.
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! - Will emit custom instructions via the [`AddCustomEntries`] and the [`add_custom_instructions`](Emitter::add_custom_instructions) function.
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//!
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! ## Usage
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//!
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//! 1. Ensure you have build scripts enabled via the `build` configuration in your `Cargo.toml`
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//!
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! ```toml
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! [package]
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! #..
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//! build = "build.rs"
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! ```
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//!
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//! 2. Add `vergen` as a build dependency in `Cargo.toml`, specifying the features you wish to enable.
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//!
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! ```toml
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! [dependencies]
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! #..
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//!
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! [build-dependencies]
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! # All features enabled
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! vergen = { version = "10", features = ["build", "cargo", "rustc", "si"] }
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//! # or
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! vergen = { version = "10", features = ["build"] }
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! # if you wish to disable certain features
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! ```
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//!
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! 3. Create a `build.rs` file that uses `vergen` to emit cargo instructions.  Configuration
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//!    starts with [`Emitter`].  Eventually you will call [`emit`](Emitter::emit) to output the
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//!    cargo instructions. See the [`emit`](Emitter::emit) documentation for more robust examples.
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//!
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//! #### Generate all output
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//!
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//! ```
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! # use anyhow::Result;
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//! # use vergen::Emitter;
[60](https://docs.rs#60)#![cfg_attr(feature = "build", doc = r"# use vergen::Build;")]
[61](https://docs.rs#61)#![cfg_attr(feature = "cargo", doc = r"# use vergen::Cargo;")]
[62](https://docs.rs#62)#![cfg_attr(feature = "rustc", doc = r"# use vergen::Rustc;")]
[63](https://docs.rs#63)#![cfg_attr(feature = "si", doc = r"# use vergen::Sysinfo;")]
[64](https://docs.rs#64)#![cfg_attr(feature = "cargo", doc = r"# use test_util::with_cargo_vars;")]
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//! #
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//! # pub fn main() -> Result<()> {
[67](https://docs.rs#67)#![cfg_attr(feature = "cargo", doc = r"# let result = with_cargo_vars(|| {")]
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//! // NOTE: This will output everything, and requires all features enabled.
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//! // NOTE: See the specific builder documentation for configuration options.
[70](https://docs.rs#70)#![cfg_attr(feature = "build", doc = r"let build = Build::all_build();")]
[71](https://docs.rs#71)#![cfg_attr(feature = "cargo", doc = r"let cargo = Cargo::all_cargo();")]
[72](https://docs.rs#72)#![cfg_attr(feature = "rustc", doc = r"let rustc = Rustc::all_rustc();")]
[73](https://docs.rs#73)#![cfg_attr(feature = "si", doc = r"let si = Sysinfo::all_sysinfo();")]
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//!
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//! Emitter::default()
[76](https://docs.rs#76)#![cfg_attr(feature = "build", doc = r"    .add_instructions(&build)?")]
[77](https://docs.rs#77)#![cfg_attr(feature = "cargo", doc = r"    .add_instructions(&cargo)?")]
[78](https://docs.rs#78)#![cfg_attr(feature = "rustc", doc = r"    .add_instructions(&rustc)?")]
[79](https://docs.rs#79)#![cfg_attr(feature = "si", doc = r"    .add_instructions(&si)?")]
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//!     .emit()?;
[81](https://docs.rs#81)#![cfg_attr(
[82](https://docs.rs#82)    feature = "cargo",
[83](https://docs.rs#83)    doc = r"
[84](https://docs.rs#84)# Ok(())
[85](https://docs.rs#85)# });
[86](https://docs.rs#86)# assert!(result.is_ok());"
[87](https://docs.rs#87))]
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//! #    Ok(())
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//! # }
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//! ```
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//! #### Sample Output
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//! ```text
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_BUILD_DATE=2024-01-31
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_BUILD_TIMESTAMP=2024-01-31T03:26:34.065893658Z
[95](https://docs.rs#95)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_CARGO_DEBUG=true
[96](https://docs.rs#96)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_CARGO_FEATURES=
[97](https://docs.rs#97)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_CARGO_OPT_LEVEL=0
[98](https://docs.rs#98)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_CARGO_TARGET_TRIPLE=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
[99](https://docs.rs#99)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_CARGO_DEPENDENCIES=anyhow 1.0.79,vergen-pretty 0.3.2
[100](https://docs.rs#100)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_RUSTC_CHANNEL=nightly
[101](https://docs.rs#101)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_RUSTC_COMMIT_DATE=2024-01-29
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_RUSTC_COMMIT_HASH=5518eaa946291f00471af8b254b2a1715f234882
[103](https://docs.rs#103)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_RUSTC_HOST_TRIPLE=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
[104](https://docs.rs#104)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_RUSTC_LLVM_VERSION=17.0
[105](https://docs.rs#105)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_RUSTC_SEMVER=1.77.0-nightly
[106](https://docs.rs#106)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_NAME=Arch Linux
[107](https://docs.rs#107)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_OS_VERSION=Linux  Arch Linux
[108](https://docs.rs#108)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_USER=jozias
[109](https://docs.rs#109)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_TOTAL_MEMORY=31 GiB
[110](https://docs.rs#110)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_VENDOR=AuthenticAMD
[111](https://docs.rs#111)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_CORE_COUNT=8
[112](https://docs.rs#112)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_NAME=cpu0,cpu1,cpu2,cpu3,cpu4,cpu5,cpu6,cpu7
[113](https://docs.rs#113)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_BRAND=AMD Ryzen Threadripper 1900X 8-Core Processor
[114](https://docs.rs#114)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_FREQUENCY=3792
[115](https://docs.rs#115)//! cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs
[116](https://docs.rs#116)//! cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT
[117](https://docs.rs#117)//! cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=VERGEN_DEFAULT_ON_ERROR
[118](https://docs.rs#118)//! cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
[119](https://docs.rs#119)//! ```
[120](https://docs.rs#120)//!
[121](https://docs.rs#121)//! #### Generate specific output
[122](https://docs.rs#122)//!
[123](https://docs.rs#123)//! ```
[124](https://docs.rs#124)//! # use anyhow::Result;
[125](https://docs.rs#125)//! # use vergen::Emitter;
[126](https://docs.rs#126)#![cfg_attr(feature = "build", doc = r"# use vergen::Build;")]
[127](https://docs.rs#127)#![cfg_attr(feature = "cargo", doc = r"# use vergen::Cargo;")]
[128](https://docs.rs#128)#![cfg_attr(feature = "rustc", doc = r"# use vergen::Rustc;")]
[129](https://docs.rs#129)#![cfg_attr(feature = "si", doc = r"# use vergen::Sysinfo;")]
[130](https://docs.rs#130)#![cfg_attr(feature = "cargo", doc = r"# use test_util::with_cargo_vars;")]
[131](https://docs.rs#131)//! #
[132](https://docs.rs#132)//! # pub fn main() -> Result<()> {
[133](https://docs.rs#133)#![cfg_attr(feature = "cargo", doc = r"# let result = with_cargo_vars(|| {")]
[134](https://docs.rs#134)#![cfg_attr(
[135](https://docs.rs#135)    feature = "build",
[136](https://docs.rs#136)    doc = r"// NOTE: This will output only the instructions specified.
[137](https://docs.rs#137)// NOTE: See the specific builder documentation for configuration options.
[138](https://docs.rs#138)let build = Build::builder().build_timestamp(true).build();"
[139](https://docs.rs#139))]
[140](https://docs.rs#140)#![cfg_attr(
[141](https://docs.rs#141)    feature = "cargo",
[142](https://docs.rs#142)    doc = r"let cargo = Cargo::builder().opt_level(true).build();"
[143](https://docs.rs#143))]
[144](https://docs.rs#144)#![cfg_attr(
[145](https://docs.rs#145)    feature = "rustc",
[146](https://docs.rs#146)    doc = r"let rustc = Rustc::builder().semver(true).build();"
[147](https://docs.rs#147))]
[148](https://docs.rs#148)#![cfg_attr(
[149](https://docs.rs#149)    feature = "si",
[150](https://docs.rs#150)    doc = r"let si = Sysinfo::builder().cpu_core_count(true).build();"
[151](https://docs.rs#151))]
[152](https://docs.rs#152)//!
[153](https://docs.rs#153)//! Emitter::default()
[154](https://docs.rs#154)#![cfg_attr(feature = "build", doc = r"    .add_instructions(&build)?")]
[155](https://docs.rs#155)#![cfg_attr(feature = "cargo", doc = r"    .add_instructions(&cargo)?")]
[156](https://docs.rs#156)#![cfg_attr(feature = "rustc", doc = r"    .add_instructions(&rustc)?")]
[157](https://docs.rs#157)#![cfg_attr(feature = "si", doc = r"    .add_instructions(&si)?")]
[158](https://docs.rs#158)//!     .emit()?;
[159](https://docs.rs#159)#![cfg_attr(
[160](https://docs.rs#160)    feature = "cargo",
[161](https://docs.rs#161)    doc = r"
[162](https://docs.rs#162)#   Ok(())
[163](https://docs.rs#163)# });
[164](https://docs.rs#164)#    assert!(result.is_ok());"
[165](https://docs.rs#165))]
[166](https://docs.rs#166)//! #   Ok(())
[167](https://docs.rs#167)//! # }
[168](https://docs.rs#168)//! ```
[169](https://docs.rs#169)//! #### Sample Output
[170](https://docs.rs#170)//! ```text
[171](https://docs.rs#171)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_BUILD_TIMESTAMP=2024-01-31T03:26:34.065893658Z
[172](https://docs.rs#172)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_CARGO_OPT_LEVEL=0
[173](https://docs.rs#173)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_RUSTC_SEMVER=1.77.0-nightly
[174](https://docs.rs#174)//! cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_CORE_COUNT=8
[175](https://docs.rs#175)//! cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs
[176](https://docs.rs#176)//! cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT
[177](https://docs.rs#177)//! cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=VERGEN_DEFAULT_ON_ERROR
[178](https://docs.rs#178)//! cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
[179](https://docs.rs#179)//! ```
[180](https://docs.rs#180)//!
[181](https://docs.rs#181)//! 4. Use the [`env!`](std::env!) or [`option_env!`](std::option_env!) macro in your code to read the environment variables.
[182](https://docs.rs#182)//!
[183](https://docs.rs#183)//! ```
[184](https://docs.rs#184)//! if let Some(timestamp) = option_env!("VERGEN_BUILD_TIMESTAMP") {
[185](https://docs.rs#185)//!     println!("Build Timestamp: {timestamp}");
[186](https://docs.rs#186)//! }
[187](https://docs.rs#187)//! if let Some(describe) = option_env!("VERGEN_GIT_DESCRIBE") {
[188](https://docs.rs#188)//!     println!("git describe: {describe}");
[189](https://docs.rs#189)//! }
[190](https://docs.rs#190)//! ```
[191](https://docs.rs#191)//!
[192](https://docs.rs#192)//! ## Features
[193](https://docs.rs#193)//! `vergen` has four main feature toggles allowing you to customize your output. No features are enabled by default.
[194](https://docs.rs#194)//! You **must** specifically enable the features you wish to use.
[195](https://docs.rs#195)#![cfg_attr(
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    feature = "emit_and_set",
[197](https://docs.rs#197)    doc = r"There is also a toggle for the [`emit_and_set`](Emitter::emit_and_set) function.  This version of emit will also set the instructions you requests as environment variables for use in `build.rs`"
[198](https://docs.rs#198))]
[199](https://docs.rs#199)//!
[200](https://docs.rs#200)//! |    Feature   | Enables                       |
[201](https://docs.rs#201)//! | ------------ | ----------------------------- |
[202](https://docs.rs#202)//! |     build    | `VERGEN_BUILD_*` instructions |
[203](https://docs.rs#203)//! |     cargo    | `VERGEN_CARGO_*` instructions |
[204](https://docs.rs#204)//! |     rustc    | `VERGEN_RUSTC_*` instructions |
[205](https://docs.rs#205)//! |      si      | `VERGEN_SYSINFO_*` instructions |
[206](https://docs.rs#206)#![cfg_attr(
[207](https://docs.rs#207)    feature = "emit_and_set",
[208](https://docs.rs#208)    doc = r"| emit_and_set | Enable the [`emit_and_set`](Emitter::emit_and_set) function |"
[209](https://docs.rs#209))]
[210](https://docs.rs#210)//!
[211](https://docs.rs#211)//! ## Environment Variables
[212](https://docs.rs#212)//! `vergen` currently recognizes the following environment variables. The full list of the environment variable names can be
[213](https://docs.rs#213)//! found as [constants here](https://docs.rs/vergen-lib/latest/vergen_lib/constants/features/index.html)
[214](https://docs.rs#214)//!
[215](https://docs.rs#215)//! | Variable | Functionality |
[216](https://docs.rs#216)//! | -------- | ------------- |
[217](https://docs.rs#217)//! | `VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT` | If this environment variable is set `vergen` will **always** use the idempotent output feature regardless of the configuration set in `build.rs`, even when the requested values could be generated normally.  This exists mainly to allow package maintainers to force idempotent output to generate deterministic binary output. |
[218](https://docs.rs#218)//! | `VERGEN_DEFAULT_ON_ERROR` | If this environment variable is set `vergen` will emit the idempotent default value for any instruction it cannot otherwise generate (e.g. `VERGEN_GIT_*` when building outside a git worktree), rather than leaving the variable unset.  Unlike `VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT`, values that *can* be generated are still emitted normally. |
[219](https://docs.rs#219)//! | `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` | If this environment variable is set `vergen` will use the value (unix time since epoch) as the basis for a time based instructions.  This can help emit deterministic instructions. |
[220](https://docs.rs#220)//! | `VERGEN_BUILD_*` | If this environment variable is set `vergen` will use the value you specify for the output rather than generating it. |
[221](https://docs.rs#221)//! | `VERGEN_CARGO_*` | If this environment variable is set `vergen` will use the value you specify for the output rather than generating it. |
[222](https://docs.rs#222)//! | `VERGEN_RUSTC_*` | If this environment variable is set `vergen` will use the value you specify for the output rather than generating it. |
[223](https://docs.rs#223)//! | `VERGEN_SYSINFO_*` | If this environment variable is set `vergen` will use the value you specify for the output rather than generating it. |
[224](https://docs.rs#224)//!
[225](https://docs.rs#225)//! ## Goals
[226](https://docs.rs#226)//! I initially wrote `vergen` (**ver**sion **gen**erator, so original) so I could embed a some git information in my
[227](https://docs.rs#227)//! personal projects.  Now, usage has grown to the point that `vergen` needs to fit better in the rust ecosystem.
[228](https://docs.rs#228)//!
[229](https://docs.rs#229)//! The current goals are as follows:
[230](https://docs.rs#230)//!
[231](https://docs.rs#231)//! #### Minimize the tool footprint
[232](https://docs.rs#232)//! - Adopt an opt-in, rather than opt-out strategy for the features.  The default feature set is empty
[233](https://docs.rs#233)//!   and no instructions will be emitted.
[234](https://docs.rs#234)//! - The instructions you have configured **will** be emitted.  If there are errors or idempotentcy
[235](https://docs.rs#235)//!   has been configured, some of those instructions may be defaulted.
[236](https://docs.rs#236)//! - Allow overriding configurtion set in `build.rs` through environment variables.  This will allow package
[237](https://docs.rs#237)//!   maintainers to force sane defaults when packaging rust binaries for distribution.
[238](https://docs.rs#238)//!
[239](https://docs.rs#239)//! #### Minimize the compile time impact
[240](https://docs.rs#240)//! - I've removed some extraneous libraries.  Any libraries added in the future will be checked against
[241](https://docs.rs#241)//!   the current standard compile times to ensure the impact is not too great.
[242](https://docs.rs#242)//! - `vergen` should compile and test from a source tarball.
[243](https://docs.rs#243)//!
[244](https://docs.rs#244)//! #### Support deterministic output
[245](https://docs.rs#245)//! Compilations run from the same source oftentimes need to generate identical binaries.  `vergen` now supports
[246](https://docs.rs#246)//! this determinism in a few ways.
[247](https://docs.rs#247)//! - An [`idempotent`](Emitter::idempotent) configuration option has been added.  When this is enabled in a
[248](https://docs.rs#248)//!   build script, each build via cargo against the same source code should generate identical binaries. Instructions
[249](https://docs.rs#249)//!   that output information that may change between builds (i.e. timestamps, sysinfo) will be defaulted.
[250](https://docs.rs#250)//! - Recognize common environment variables that support deterministic builds (i.e. [`SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`](https://reproducible-builds.org/docs/source-date-epoch/))
[251](https://docs.rs#251)//! - Allow `build.rs` configuration overrides though environment variables to allow users building a binary, but
[252](https://docs.rs#252)//!   not controlling the source to generate deterministic binaries.
[253](https://docs.rs#253)//!
[254](https://docs.rs#254)//! # Use Cases
[255](https://docs.rs#255)//! I generally use vergen for the following two cases
[256](https://docs.rs#256)//!
[257](https://docs.rs#257)//! 1. Generating verbose output describing a command line application.
[258](https://docs.rs#258)//!
[259](https://docs.rs#259)//! ```text
[260](https://docs.rs#260)//! ~/p/r/app λ app -vv
[261](https://docs.rs#261)//! app 0.1.0
[262](https://docs.rs#262)//!
[263](https://docs.rs#263)//! Build Timestamp:     2021-02-23T20:14:46.558472672+00:00
[264](https://docs.rs#264)//! rustc Version:       1.52.0-nightly
[265](https://docs.rs#265)//! rustc Channel:       nightly
[266](https://docs.rs#266)//! rustc Host Triple:   x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
[267](https://docs.rs#267)//! rustc Commit SHA:    3f5aee2d5241139d808f4fdece0026603489afd1
[268](https://docs.rs#268)//! cargo Target Triple: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
[269](https://docs.rs#269)//! cargo Profile:       release
[270](https://docs.rs#270)//! ```
[271](https://docs.rs#271)//!
[272](https://docs.rs#272)//! 2. Information endpoints in web apis
[273](https://docs.rs#273)//!
[274](https://docs.rs#274)//! ```json
[275](https://docs.rs#275)//! ~/p/r/app λ curl https://some.app.com/info | jq
[276](https://docs.rs#276)//! {
[277](https://docs.rs#277)//!   "build_timestamp": "2021-02-19T21:32:22.932833758+00:00",
[278](https://docs.rs#278)//!   "rustc_semver": "1.52.0-nightly",
[279](https://docs.rs#279)//!   "rustc_channel": "nightly",
[280](https://docs.rs#280)//!   "rustc_host_triple": "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu",
[281](https://docs.rs#281)//!   "rustc_commit_sha": "3f5aee2d5241139d808f4fdece0026603489afd1",
[282](https://docs.rs#282)//!   "cargo_target_triple": "x86_64-unknown-linux-musl",
[283](https://docs.rs#283)//!   "cargo_profile": "release"
[284](https://docs.rs#284)//! }
[285](https://docs.rs#285)//! ```
[286](https://docs.rs#286)//!
[287](https://docs.rs#287)//! [build scripts]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html#outputs-of-the-build-script
[288](https://docs.rs#288)//! [cargo:rustc-env]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html#rustc-env
[289](https://docs.rs#289)//! [cargo:rerun-if-changed]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html#rerun-if-changed
[290](https://docs.rs#290)//!
[291](https://docs.rs#291)

# Emitter in vergen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vergen/10.0.1/vergen/struct.Emitter.html

`pub struct Emitter { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The `Emitter` will emit cargo instructions (i.e. cargo:rustc-env=NAME=VALUE)
base on the configuration you enable.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/vergen-lib/10.0.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/vergen_lib/emitter.rs.html#127)#### pub fn [idempotent](https://docs.rs#method.idempotent)(&mut self) -> &mut [Emitter](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/vergen-lib/10.0.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/vergen_lib/emitter.rs.html#127)

#### pub fn [idempotent](https://docs.rs#method.idempotent)(&mut self) -> &mut [Emitter](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)

Enable the `idempotent` feature

**NOTE** - This feature can also be enabled via the `VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT`
environment variable.

When this feature is enabled, certain vergen output (i.e. timestamps, sysinfo)
will be set to an idempotent default.  This will allow systems that
depend on deterministic builds to override user requested `vergen`
impurities.  This will mainly allow for package maintainers to build
packages that depend on `vergen` in a deterministic manner.

See [this issue](https://github.com/rustyhorde/vergen/issues/141) for
more details

| Variable | Sample |
|---|---|
| `VERGEN_BUILD_DATE` | `VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT_OUTPUT` |
| `VERGEN_BUILD_TIMESTAMP` | `VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT_OUTPUT` |

**NOTE** - This feature **always** forces idempotent output, even when the
requested instructions *could* be generated normally (e.g. inside a real git
worktree).  Use it only when you want deterministic builds.  If you instead
want real values when they are available but a default placeholder only when
generation fails (e.g. building outside a git worktree), use
[ default_on_error](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html#method.default_on_error) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
Emitter::new().idempotent().emit()?;
// or
// set::env("VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT", "true");
Emitter::new().emit()?;
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/vergen-lib/10.0.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/vergen_lib/emitter.rs.html#170)#### pub fn [default_on_error](https://docs.rs#method.default_on_error)(&mut self) -> &mut [Emitter](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/vergen-lib/10.0.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/vergen_lib/emitter.rs.html#170)

#### pub fn [default_on_error](https://docs.rs#method.default_on_error)(&mut self) -> &mut [Emitter](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)

Enable the `default_on_error` feature

**NOTE** - This feature can also be enabled via the `VERGEN_DEFAULT_ON_ERROR`
environment variable.

By default, if `vergen` cannot generate a requested instruction (for example
when you configure `VERGEN_GIT_*` instructions but build from a source tarball
with no `.git` directory), the variable is left **unset** and only a
[ cargo:warning](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html#cargo-warning)
is emitted.  This means a downstream

`env!("VERGEN_GIT_SHA")` will fail to
compile.When this feature is enabled, those un-generatable instructions are instead
populated with the idempotent default value (`VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT_OUTPUT`), so
`env!()` keeps compiling.  Unlike [ idempotent](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html#method.idempotent), this only
affects the fallback path: when the instructions

*can*be generated (e.g. inside a real git worktree) you still get the real values.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

```
Emitter::new().default_on_error().emit()?;
// or
// set::env("VERGEN_DEFAULT_ON_ERROR", "true");
Emitter::new().emit()?;
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/vergen-lib/10.0.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/vergen_lib/emitter.rs.html#203)#### pub fn [fail_on_error](https://docs.rs#method.fail_on_error)(&mut self) -> &mut [Emitter](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/vergen-lib/10.0.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/vergen_lib/emitter.rs.html#203)

#### pub fn [fail_on_error](https://docs.rs#method.fail_on_error)(&mut self) -> &mut [Emitter](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)

Enable the `fail_on_error` feature

By default `vergen` will emit the instructions you requested.  If for some
reason those instructions cannot be generated correctly, the affected variables
are left unset (unless [ idempotent](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html#method.idempotent) or

[is enabled, in which case they are populated with the idempotent default value).](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html#method.default_on_error)

`default_on_error``vergen` will also emit
[instructions notifying you this has happened.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html#cargo-warning)

`cargo:warning`For example, if you configure `vergen` to emit `VERGEN_GIT_*` instructions and
you run a build from a source tarball with no `.git` directory, the instructions
will be skipped (or defaulted, per above), rather than information gleaned through
git.

When `fail_on_error` is enabled, that situation produces a hard error instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example

`Emitter::new().fail_on_error().emit()?;`[Source](https://docs.rs/vergen-lib/10.0.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/vergen_lib/emitter.rs.html#245)#### pub fn [custom_build_rs](https://docs.rs#method.custom_build_rs)(&mut self, path: &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> &mut [Emitter](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/vergen-lib/10.0.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/vergen_lib/emitter.rs.html#245)

#### pub fn [custom_build_rs](https://docs.rs#method.custom_build_rs)(&mut self, path: &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> &mut [Emitter](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html)

Set a custom build.rs path if you are using a non-standard path

By default `vergen` will use `build.rs` as the build path for the
`cargo:rerun-if-changed` emit.  You can specify a custom `build.rs`
path here if you have changed this default

[§](https://docs.rs#example-4)Example

`Emitter::new().custom_build_rs("my/custom/build.rs").emit()?;`Emit cargo instructions from your build script

- Will emit `cargo:rustc-env=VAR=VALUE`
- Will emit `cargo:rerun-if-changed=PATH`
- Can emit `cargo:warning``fail_on_error``idempotent`

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-2)Errors

- The `writeln!``std::io::Error`

[§](https://docs.rs#example-5)Example

`let emitter = Emitter::default().emit()?;`[§](https://docs.rs#sample-output)Sample Output

The instruction output is not displayed by default.

[Source](https://docs.rs/vergen-lib/10.0.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/vergen_lib/emitter.rs.html#476)#### pub fn [emit_and_set](https://docs.rs#method.emit_and_set)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [Error](https://docs.rs/anyhow/1.0.102/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/anyhow/struct.Error.html)>

**crate feature **`emit_and_set` only.

[Source](https://docs.rs/vergen-lib/10.0.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/vergen_lib/emitter.rs.html#476)

#### pub fn [emit_and_set](https://docs.rs#method.emit_and_set)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [Error](https://docs.rs/anyhow/1.0.102/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/anyhow/struct.Error.html)>

**crate feature**only.

`emit_and_set`Emit cargo instructions from your build script and set environment variables for use in `build.rs`

- Will emit `cargo:rustc-env=VAR=VALUE`
- Will emit `cargo:rerun-if-changed=PATH`
- Can emit `cargo:warning``fail_on_error``idempotent`

# AddCustomEntries in vergen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vergen/10.0.1/vergen/trait.AddCustomEntries.html

```
pub trait AddCustomEntries<K, V>{
    // Required methods
    fn
```
[add_calculated_entries](https://docs.rs#tymethod.add_calculated_entries)(
        &self,
        idempotent: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
        cargo_rustc_env_map: &mut [BTreeMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/collections/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html)<K, V>,
        cargo_rerun_if_changed: &mut [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
        cargo_warning: &mut [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
    ) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [Error](https://docs.rs/anyhow/1.0.102/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/anyhow/struct.Error.html)>;

        &self,
        config: &[DefaultConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.DefaultConfig.html),
        cargo_rustc_env_map: &mut [BTreeMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/collections/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html)<K, V>,
        cargo_rerun_if_changed: &mut [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
        cargo_warning: &mut [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
    ) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [Error](https://docs.rs/anyhow/1.0.102/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/anyhow/struct.Error.html)>;
}## Expand description

This trait should be implemented to allow the `vergen` emitter to properly emit your custom instructions.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
#[derive(Default)]
struct Custom {}
impl AddCustomEntries<&str, &str> for Custom {
    fn add_calculated_entries(
        &self,
        _idempotent: bool,
        cargo_rustc_env_map: &mut BTreeMap<&str, &str>,
        _cargo_rerun_if_changed: &mut CargoRerunIfChanged,
        cargo_warning: &mut CargoWarning,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        cargo_rustc_env_map.insert("vergen-cl", "custom_instruction");
        cargo_warning.push("custom instruction generated".to_string());
        Ok(())
    }
    fn add_default_entries(
        &self,
        _config: &DefaultConfig,
        _cargo_rustc_env_map: &mut BTreeMap<&str, &str>,
        _cargo_rerun_if_changed: &mut CargoRerunIfChanged,
        _cargo_warning: &mut CargoWarning,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#then-in-buildrs)Then in [`build.rs`]

```
let build = BuildBuilder::all_build()?;
let cargo = CargoBuilder::all_cargo()?;
let gix = GixBuilder::all_git()?;
let rustc = RustcBuilder::all_rustc()?;
let si = SysinfoBuilder::all_sysinfo()?;
Emitter::default()
    .add_instructions(&build)?
    .add_instructions(&cargo)?
    .add_instructions(&gix)?
    .add_instructions(&rustc)?
    .add_instructions(&si)?
    .add_custom_instructions(&Custom::default())?
    .emit()
```
## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/vergen-lib/10.0.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/vergen_lib/entries.rs.html#155-161)

[Source](https://docs.rs/vergen-lib/10.0.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/vergen_lib/entries.rs.html#155-161)

Try to add instructions entries to the various given arguments.

- Write to the `cargo_rustc_env`map to emit ‘cargo:rustc-env=NAME=VALUE’ instructions.
- Write to the `cargo_rerun_if_changed`vector to emit ‘cargo:rerun-if-changed=VALUE’ instructions.
- Write to the `cargo_warning`vector to emit ‘cargo:warning=VALUE’ instructions.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

If an error occurs, the `vergen` emitter will use `add_default_entries` to generate output.
This assumes generating instructions may fail in some manner so a [ anyhow::Result](https://docs.rs/anyhow/1.0.102/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/anyhow/type.Result.html) is returned.

[Source](https://docs.rs/vergen-lib/10.0.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/vergen_lib/entries.rs.html#173-179)#### fn [add_default_entries](https://docs.rs#tymethod.add_default_entries)(
    &self,
    config: &[DefaultConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.DefaultConfig.html),
    cargo_rustc_env_map: &mut [BTreeMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/collections/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html)<K, V>,
    cargo_rerun_if_changed: &mut [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
    cargo_warning: &mut [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [Error](https://docs.rs/anyhow/1.0.102/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/anyhow/struct.Error.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/vergen-lib/10.0.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/vergen_lib/entries.rs.html#173-179)

#### fn [add_default_entries](https://docs.rs#tymethod.add_default_entries)(
    &self,
    config: &[DefaultConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.DefaultConfig.html),
    cargo_rustc_env_map: &mut [BTreeMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/collections/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html)<K, V>,
    cargo_rerun_if_changed: &mut [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
    cargo_warning: &mut [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [Error](https://docs.rs/anyhow/1.0.102/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/anyhow/struct.Error.html)>

Based on the given configuration, emit either default idempotent output or generate a failue.

- Write to the `cargo_rustc_env`map to emit ‘cargo:rustc-env=NAME=VALUE’ instructions.
- Write to the `cargo_rerun_if_changed`vector to emit ‘cargo:rerun-if-changed=VALUE’ instructions.
- Write to the `cargo_warning`vector to emit ‘cargo:warning=VALUE’ instructions.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-1)Errors

This assumes generating instructions may fail in some manner so a [ anyhow::Result](https://docs.rs/anyhow/1.0.102/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/anyhow/type.Result.html) is returned.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# Build in vergen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vergen/10.0.1/vergen/struct.Build.html

`pub struct Build { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`build`## Expand description

The `VERGEN_BUILD_*` configuration features

| Variable | Sample |
|---|---|
| `VERGEN_BUILD_DATE` | 2021-02-25 |
| `VERGEN_BUILD_TIMESTAMP` | 2021-02-25T23:28:39.493201+00:00 |

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Emit all of the build instructions

```
let build = Build::all_build();
Emitter::new().add_instructions(&build)?.emit()?;
```
Emit some of the build instructions

```
let build = Build::builder().build_timestamp(true).build();
Emitter::new().add_instructions(&build)?.emit()?;
```
Override output with your own value

```
temp_env::with_var("VERGEN_BUILD_DATE", Some("01/01/2023"), || {
    let result = || -> Result<()> {
        let build = Build::builder().build_date(true).build();
        Emitter::new().add_instructions(&build)?.emit()?;
        Ok(())
    }();
    assert!(result.is_ok());
});
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

This feature can also be used in conjuction with the [ SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH](https://reproducible-builds.org/docs/source-date-epoch/)
environment variable to generate deterministic timestamps based off the
last modification time of the source/package

```
temp_env::with_var("SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH", Some("1671809360"), || {
    let result = || -> Result<()> {
        let build = Build::all_build();
        Emitter::new().add_instructions(&build)?.emit()?;
        Ok(())
    }();
});
```
The above will always generate the following output for the timestamp related instructions

```
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_BUILD_DATE=2022-12-23
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_BUILD_TIMESTAMP=2022-12-23T15:29:20.000000000Z
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example

This feature also recognizes the idempotent flag.

**NOTE** - `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` takes precedence over the idempotent flag. If you
use both, the output will be based off `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`.  This would still be
deterministic.

```
let build = Build::builder().build();
Emitter::new().idempotent().add_instructions(&build)?.emit()?;
```
The above will always generate the following output for the timestamp related instructions unless you also use quiet, then the warnings will be suppressed.

```
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_BUILD_DATE=VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT_OUTPUT
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_BUILD_TIMESTAMP=VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT_OUTPUT
cargo:warning=VERGEN_BUILD_DATE set to default
cargo:warning=VERGEN_BUILD_TIMESTAMP set to default
cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs
cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT
cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=VERGEN_DEFAULT_ON_ERROR
cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
```

# Cargo in vergen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vergen/10.0.1/vergen/struct.Cargo.html

`pub struct Cargo { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`cargo`## Expand description

Configure the emission of `VERGEN_CARGO_*` instructions

**NOTE** - All cargo instructions are considered deterministic.  If you change
the version of cargo you are compiling with, these values should change if
being used in the generated binary.

| Variable | Sample |
|---|---|
| `VERGEN_CARGO_DEBUG` | true |
| `VERGEN_CARGO_FEATURES` | git,build |
| `VERGEN_CARGO_OPT_LEVEL` | 1 |
| `VERGEN_CARGO_TARGET_TRIPLE` | x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu |

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Emit all of the cargo instructions

```
fn main() -> Result<()> {
    temp_env::with_vars([
        ("CARGO_FEATURE_BUILD", Some("")),
        ("DEBUG", Some("true")),
        ("OPT_LEVEL", Some("1")),
        ("TARGET", Some("x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"))
    ], || {
        let cargo = Cargo::all_cargo();
        Emitter::default().add_instructions(&cargo)?.emit()?;
    });
```
Emit some of the cargo instructions

```
    temp_env::with_vars([
        ("OPT_LEVEL", Some("1")),
        ("TARGET", Some("x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"))
    ], || {
        let cargo = Cargo::builder().opt_level(true).build();
        Emitter::default().add_instructions(&cargo)?.emit()?;
    });
```
Override output with your own value

```
fn main() -> Result<()> {
    temp_env::with_vars([
        ("CARGO_FEATURE_BUILD", Some("")),
        ("VERGEN_CARGO_DEBUG", Some("my own debug value")),
        ("OPT_LEVEL", Some("1")),
        ("TARGET", Some("x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"))
     ], || {
         let cargo = Cargo::all_cargo();
         Emitter::default().add_instructions(&cargo)?.emit()?;
     });
```

# CpuRefreshKind in vergen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vergen/10.0.1/vergen/struct.CpuRefreshKind.html

`pub struct CpuRefreshKind { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`si`## Expand description

Used to determine what you want to refresh specifically on the [ Cpu](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sysinfo/common/system/struct.Cpu.html) type.

⚠️ Just like all other refresh types, ruling out a refresh doesn’t assure you that the information won’t be retrieved if the information is accessible without needing extra computation.

```
use sysinfo::{CpuRefreshKind, System};
let mut system = System::new();
// We don't want to update all the CPU information.
system.refresh_cpu_specifics(CpuRefreshKind::everything().without_frequency());
for cpu in system.cpus() {
    assert_eq!(cpu.frequency(), 0);
}
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/sysinfo/common/system.rs.html#2573)#### pub fn [nothing](https://docs.rs#method.nothing)() -> [CpuRefreshKind](https://docs.rs/struct.CpuRefreshKind.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/sysinfo/common/system.rs.html#2573)

assert_eq!(r.cpu_usage(), false);
```

```

# MemoryRefreshKind in vergen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vergen/10.0.1/vergen/struct.MemoryRefreshKind.html

`pub struct MemoryRefreshKind { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`si`## Expand description

Used to determine which memory you want to refresh specifically.

⚠️ Just like all other refresh types, ruling out a refresh doesn’t assure you that the information won’t be retrieved if the information is accessible without needing extra computation.

```
use sysinfo::{MemoryRefreshKind, System};
let mut system = System::new();
// We don't want to update all memories information.
system.refresh_memory_specifics(MemoryRefreshKind::nothing().with_ram());
println!("total RAM: {}", system.total_memory());
println!("free RAM:  {}", system.free_memory());
```

# ProcessRefreshKind in vergen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vergen/10.0.1/vergen/struct.ProcessRefreshKind.html

`pub struct ProcessRefreshKind { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`si`## Expand description

Used to determine what you want to refresh specifically on the [ Process](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sysinfo/common/system/struct.Process.html) type.

When all refresh are ruled out, a [ Process](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sysinfo/common/system/struct.Process.html) will still retrieve the following information:

- Process ID (`Pid`
- Parent process ID (on Windows it never changes though)
- Process name
- Start time

⚠️ Just like all other refresh types, ruling out a refresh doesn’t assure you that the information won’t be retrieved if the information is accessible without needing extra computation.

⚠️ ** Linux Specific ** ⚠️
When using `ProcessRefreshKind::everything()`, in linux we will fetch all relevant
information from `/proc/<pid>/` as well as all the information from `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/`
folders. This makes the refresh mechanism a lot slower depending on the number of tasks
each process has.

If you don’t care about tasks information, use `ProcessRefreshKind::everything().without_tasks()`
as much as possible.

```
use sysinfo::{ProcessesToUpdate, ProcessRefreshKind, System};
let mut system = System::new();
// We don't want to update the CPU information.
system.refresh_processes_specifics(
    ProcessesToUpdate::All,
    true,
    ProcessRefreshKind::everything().without_cpu(),
);
for (_, proc_) in system.processes() {
    // We use a `==` comparison on float only because we know it's set to 0 here.
    assert_eq!(proc_.cpu_usage(), 0.);
}
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/sysinfo/common/system.rs.html#2457)#### pub fn [nothing](https://docs.rs#method.nothing)() -> [ProcessRefreshKind](https://docs.rs/struct.ProcessRefreshKind.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/sysinfo/common/system.rs.html#2457)

#### pub fn [nothing](https://docs.rs#method.nothing)() -> [ProcessRefreshKind](https://docs.rs/struct.ProcessRefreshKind.html)

Creates a new `ProcessRefreshKind` with every refresh set to `false`, except for `tasks`.
By default, we want to list all processes and tasks are considered processes on their own
in linux so we still fetch them by default. However, the processes information are not
refreshed.

```
use sysinfo::{ProcessRefreshKind, UpdateKind};
let r = ProcessRefreshKind::nothing();
assert_eq!(r.cpu(), false);
assert_eq!(r.user(), UpdateKind::Never);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/sysinfo/common/system.rs.html#2472)#### pub fn [everything](https://docs.rs#method.everything)() -> [ProcessRefreshKind](https://docs.rs/struct.ProcessRefreshKind.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/sysinfo/common/system.rs.html#2472)

#### pub fn [everything](https://docs.rs#method.everything)() -> [ProcessRefreshKind](https://docs.rs/struct.ProcessRefreshKind.html)

Creates a new `ProcessRefreshKind` with every refresh set to `true` or
[ UpdateKind::OnlyIfNotSet](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sysinfo/common/system/enum.UpdateKind.html#variant.OnlyIfNotSet).

```
use sysinfo::{ProcessRefreshKind, UpdateKind};
let r = ProcessRefreshKind::everything();
assert_eq!(r.cpu(), true);
assert_eq!(r.user(), UpdateKind::OnlyIfNotSet);
```
Returns the value of the “cpu” refresh kind. It will retrieve both CPU usage and CPU accumulated time,

```
use sysinfo::ProcessRefreshKind;
let r = ProcessRefreshKind::nothing();
let r = r.with_cpu();
assert_eq!(r.cpu(), true);
let r = r.without_cpu();
assert_eq!(r.cpu(), false);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/sysinfo/common/system.rs.html#2487-2494)

[Source](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/sysinfo/common/system.rs.html#2501-2514)#### pub fn [user](https://docs.rs#method.user)(&self) -> [UpdateKind](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sysinfo/common/system/enum.UpdateKind.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/sysinfo/common/system.rs.html#2501-2514)

#### pub fn [user](https://docs.rs#method.user)(&self) -> [UpdateKind](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sysinfo/common/system/enum.UpdateKind.html)

Returns the value of the “user” refresh kind. It will retrieve the following information:

- user ID
- user effective ID (if available on the platform)
- user group ID (if available on the platform)
- user effective ID (if available on the platform)

```
use sysinfo::{ProcessRefreshKind, UpdateKind};
let r = ProcessRefreshKind::nothing();
assert_eq!(r.user(), UpdateKind::Never);
let r = r.with_user(UpdateKind::OnlyIfNotSet);
assert_eq!(r.user(), UpdateKind::OnlyIfNotSet);
let r = r.without_user();
assert_eq!(r.user(), UpdateKind::Never);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/sysinfo/common/system.rs.html#2501-2514)#### pub fn [with_user](https://docs.rs#method.with_user)(self, kind: [UpdateKind](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sysinfo/common/system/enum.UpdateKind.html)) -> [ProcessRefreshKind](https://docs.rs/struct.ProcessRefreshKind.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/sysinfo/common/system.rs.html#2501-2514)

Sets the value of the “exe” refresh kind to `UpdateKind::Never`.

```
use sysinfo::{ProcessRefreshKind, UpdateKind};
let r = ProcessRefreshKind::everything();
assert_eq!(r.exe(), UpdateKind::OnlyIfNotSet);
let r = r.without_exe();
assert_eq!(r.exe(), UpdateKind::Never);
```

assert_eq!(r.tasks(), true);
let r = r.without_tasks();
assert_eq!(r.tasks(), false);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/sysinfo/common/system.rs.html#2427)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Default-for-ProcessRefreshKind)### impl [Default](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/default/trait.Default.html) for [ProcessRefreshKind](https://docs.rs/struct.ProcessRefreshKind.html)

Creates a new `ProcessRefreshKind` with every refresh set to `false`, except for `tasks`.
By default, we want to list all processes and tasks are considered processes on their own
in linux so we still fetch them by default. However, the processes information are not
refreshed.

[Source](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/sysinfo/common/system.rs.html#2427)

# RefreshKind in vergen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vergen/10.0.1/vergen/struct.RefreshKind.html

`pub struct RefreshKind { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`si`## Expand description

Used to determine what you want to refresh specifically on the [ System](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sysinfo/common/system/struct.System.html) type.

⚠️ Just like all other refresh types, ruling out a refresh doesn’t assure you that the information won’t be retrieved if the information is accessible without needing extra computation.

```
use sysinfo::{RefreshKind, System};
// We want everything except memory.
let mut system = System::new_with_specifics(RefreshKind::everything().without_memory());
assert_eq!(system.total_memory(), 0);
assert!(system.processes().len() > 0);
```

```
use sysinfo::RefreshKind;

assert_eq!(r.processes().is_some(), false);
assert_eq!(r.memory().is_some(), false);
assert_eq!(r.cpu().is_some(), false);
```

# Rustc in vergen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vergen/10.0.1/vergen/struct.Rustc.html

`pub struct Rustc { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`rustc`## Expand description

The `VERGEN_RUSTC_*` configuration features

**NOTE** - All rustc instructions are considered deterministic.  If you change
the version of rustc you are compiling with, these values should change if
being used in the generated binary.

| Variable | Sample |
|---|---|
| `VERGEN_RUSTC_CHANNEL` | nightly |
| `VERGEN_RUSTC_COMMIT_DATE` | 2021-02-24 |
| `VERGEN_RUSTC_COMMIT_HASH` | a8486b64b0c87dabd045453b6c81500015d122d6 |
| `VERGEN_RUSTC_HOST_TRIPLE` | apple-darwin |
| `VERGEN_RUSTC_LLVM_VERSION` | 11.0 |
| `VERGEN_RUSTC_SEMVER` | 1.52.0-nightly |

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Emit all of the rustc instructions

```
let rustc = Rustc::all_rustc();
Emitter::default().add_instructions(&rustc)?.emit();
```
Emit some of the rustc instructions

```
let rustc = Rustc::builder().channel(true).semver(true).build();
Emitter::default().add_instructions(&rustc)?.emit();
```
Override output with your own value

```
temp_env::with_var("VERGEN_RUSTC_CHANNEL", Some("this is the channel I want output"), || {
    let result = || -> Result<()> {
        let rustc = Rustc::builder().channel(true).semver(true).build();
        Emitter::default().add_instructions(&rustc)?.emit();
        Ok(())
    }();
    assert!(result.is_ok());
});
```

# Sysinfo in vergen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vergen/10.0.1/vergen/struct.Sysinfo.html

`pub struct Sysinfo { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`si`## Expand description

The `VERGEN_SYSINFO_*` configuration features

| Variable | Sample |
|---|---|
| `VERGEN_SYSINFO_NAME` | Manjaro Linux |
| `VERGEN_SYSINFO_OS_VERSION` | Linux Manjaro Linux |
| `VERGEN_SYSINFO_USER` | Yoda |
| `VERGEN_SYSINFO_TOTAL_MEMORY` | 33 GB |
| `VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_VENDOR` | Authentic AMD |
| `VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_CORE_COUNT` | 8 |
| `VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_NAME` | cpu0,cpu1,cpu2,cpu3,cpu4,cpu5,cpu6,cpu7 |
| `VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_BRAND` | AMD Ryzen Threadripper 1900X 8-Core Processor |
| `VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_FREQUENCY` | 3792 |

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Emit all sysinfo instructions

```
let si = Sysinfo::all_sysinfo();
Emitter::default().add_instructions(&si)?.emit()?;
```
Emit some of the sysinfo instructions

```
let si = Sysinfo::builder().os_version(true).cpu_core_count(true).build();
Emitter::default()
    .add_instructions(&si)?
    .emit()?;
```
Override output with your own value

```
temp_env::with_var("VERGEN_SYSINFO_NAME", Some("this is the name I want output"), || {
    let result = || -> Result<()> {
        let si = Sysinfo::all_sysinfo();
        Emitter::default().add_instructions(&si)?.emit()?;
        Ok(())
    }();
    assert!(result.is_ok());
});
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

This feature also recognizes the idempotent flag.

```
let si = Sysinfo::all_sysinfo();
Emitter::default().idempotent().add_instructions(&si)?.emit()?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example

Use `refresh_kind` to minimize the amount of data that [ sysinfo](https://docs.rs/sysinfo/0.39.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sysinfo/index.html) refreshes.

```
let refresh_kind = RefreshKind::nothing();
let cpu_refresh_kind = CpuRefreshKind::everything()
    .without_cpu_usage()
    .without_frequency();
let si = Sysinfo::builder()
    .cpu_brand(true)
    .refresh_kind(refresh_kind.with_cpu(cpu_refresh_kind))
    .build();
let config = Emitter::default()
    .add_instructions(&si)?
    .emit()?;
```
The above will always generate the following output

```
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_NAME=VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT_OUTPUT
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_OS_VERSION=VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT_OUTPUT
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_USER=VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT_OUTPUT
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_TOTAL_MEMORY=VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT_OUTPUT
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_VENDOR=VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT_OUTPUT
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_CORE_COUNT=VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT_OUTPUT
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_NAME=VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT_OUTPUT
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_BRAND=VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT_OUTPUT
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_FREQUENCY=VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT_OUTPUT
cargo:warning=VERGEN_SYSINFO_NAME set to default
cargo:warning=VERGEN_SYSINFO_OS_VERSION set to default
cargo:warning=VERGEN_SYSINFO_USER set to default
cargo:warning=VERGEN_SYSINFO_TOTAL_MEMORY set to default
cargo:warning=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_VENDOR set to default
cargo:warning=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_CORE_COUNT set to default
cargo:warning=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_NAME set to default
cargo:warning=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_BRAND set to default
cargo:warning=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_FREQUENCY set to default
cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs
cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT
cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=VERGEN_DEFAULT_ON_ERROR
cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
```

# vergen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vergen/latest/vergen/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#vergen---emit-cargo-instructions-from-a-build-script)vergen - Emit cargo instructions from a build script

`vergen`, when used in conjunction with cargo [build scripts](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html#outputs-of-the-build-script) can emit the following:

- Will emit `cargo:rustc-env=VAR=VALUE``env`!`option_env`!
- Can emit `cargo:warning``fail_on_error``idempotent`
- Will emit `cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs``build.rs`file changed.
- Will emit `cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT``VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT`environment variable has changed.
- Will emit `cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=VERGEN_DEFAULT_ON_ERROR``VERGEN_DEFAULT_ON_ERROR`environment variable has changed.
- Will emit `cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH``SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`environment variable has changed.
- Will emit custom instructions via the `AddCustomEntries``add_custom_instructions`

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

- Ensure you have build scripts enabled via the `build`configuration in your`Cargo.toml`

```
[package]
#..
build = "build.rs"
```
- Add `vergen`as a build dependency in`Cargo.toml`, specifying the features you wish to enable.

```
[dependencies]
#..
[build-dependencies]
# All features enabled
vergen = { version = "10", features = ["build", "cargo", "rustc", "si"] }
# or
vergen = { version = "10", features = ["build"] }
# if you wish to disable certain features
```
- Create a `build.rs`file that uses`vergen`to emit cargo instructions. Configuration starts with`Emitter``emit``emit`

[§](https://docs.rs#generate-all-output)Generate all output

```
// NOTE: This will output everything, and requires all features enabled.
// NOTE: See the specific builder documentation for configuration options.
let build = Build::all_build();
let cargo = Cargo::all_cargo();
let rustc = Rustc::all_rustc();
let si = Sysinfo::all_sysinfo();
Emitter::default()
    .add_instructions(&build)?
    .add_instructions(&cargo)?
    .add_instructions(&rustc)?
    .add_instructions(&si)?
    .emit()?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#sample-output)Sample Output

```
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_BUILD_DATE=2024-01-31
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_BUILD_TIMESTAMP=2024-01-31T03:26:34.065893658Z
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_CARGO_DEBUG=true
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_CARGO_FEATURES=
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_CARGO_OPT_LEVEL=0
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_CARGO_TARGET_TRIPLE=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_CARGO_DEPENDENCIES=anyhow 1.0.79,vergen-pretty 0.3.2
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_RUSTC_CHANNEL=nightly
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_RUSTC_COMMIT_DATE=2024-01-29
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_RUSTC_COMMIT_HASH=5518eaa946291f00471af8b254b2a1715f234882
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_RUSTC_HOST_TRIPLE=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_RUSTC_LLVM_VERSION=17.0
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_RUSTC_SEMVER=1.77.0-nightly
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_NAME=Arch Linux
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_OS_VERSION=Linux  Arch Linux
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_USER=jozias
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_TOTAL_MEMORY=31 GiB
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_VENDOR=AuthenticAMD
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_CORE_COUNT=8
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_NAME=cpu0,cpu1,cpu2,cpu3,cpu4,cpu5,cpu6,cpu7
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_BRAND=AMD Ryzen Threadripper 1900X 8-Core Processor
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_FREQUENCY=3792
cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs
cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT
cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=VERGEN_DEFAULT_ON_ERROR
cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
```
[§](https://docs.rs#generate-specific-output)Generate specific output

```
// NOTE: This will output only the instructions specified.
// NOTE: See the specific builder documentation for configuration options.
let build = Build::builder().build_timestamp(true).build();
let cargo = Cargo::builder().opt_level(true).build();
let rustc = Rustc::builder().semver(true).build();
let si = Sysinfo::builder().cpu_core_count(true).build();
Emitter::default()
    .add_instructions(&build)?
    .add_instructions(&cargo)?
    .add_instructions(&rustc)?
    .add_instructions(&si)?
    .emit()?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#sample-output-1)Sample Output

```
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_BUILD_TIMESTAMP=2024-01-31T03:26:34.065893658Z
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_CARGO_OPT_LEVEL=0
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_RUSTC_SEMVER=1.77.0-nightly
cargo:rustc-env=VERGEN_SYSINFO_CPU_CORE_COUNT=8
cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs
cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT
cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=VERGEN_DEFAULT_ON_ERROR
cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
```
- Use the `env!``option_env!`

```
if let Some(timestamp) = option_env!("VERGEN_BUILD_TIMESTAMP") {
    println!("Build Timestamp: {timestamp}");
}
if let Some(describe) = option_env!("VERGEN_GIT_DESCRIBE") {
    println!("git describe: {describe}");
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

`vergen` has four main feature toggles allowing you to customize your output. No features are enabled by default.
You **must** specifically enable the features you wish to use.

There is also a toggle for the [ emit_and_set](https://docs.rs/struct.Emitter.html#method.emit_and_set) function.  This version of emit will also set the instructions you requests as environment variables for use in

`build.rs`| Feature | Enables |
|---|---|
| build | `VERGEN_BUILD_*`instructions |
| cargo | `VERGEN_CARGO_*`instructions |
| rustc | `VERGEN_RUSTC_*`instructions |
| si | `VERGEN_SYSINFO_*`instructions |
| emit_and_set | Enable the function`emit_and_set` |

[§](https://docs.rs#environment-variables)Environment Variables

`vergen` currently recognizes the following environment variables. The full list of the environment variable names can be
found as [constants here](https://docs.rs/vergen-lib/latest/vergen_lib/constants/features/index.html)

| Variable | Functionality |
|---|---|
| `VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT` | If this environment variable is set `vergen`willalwaysuse the idempotent output feature regardless of the configuration set in`build.rs`, even when the requested values could be generated normally.  This exists mainly to allow package maintainers to force idempotent output to generate deterministic binary output. |
| `VERGEN_DEFAULT_ON_ERROR` | If this environment variable is set `vergen`will emit the idempotent default value for any instruction it cannot otherwise generate (e.g.`VERGEN_GIT_*`when building outside a git worktree), rather than leaving the variable unset.  Unlike`VERGEN_IDEMPOTENT`, values thatcanbe generated are still emitted normally. |
| `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` | If this environment variable is set `vergen`will use the value (unix time since epoch) as the basis for a time based instructions.  This can help emit deterministic instructions. |
| `VERGEN_BUILD_*` | If this environment variable is set `vergen`will use the value you specify for the output rather than generating it. |
| `VERGEN_CARGO_*` | If this environment variable is set `vergen`will use the value you specify for the output rather than generating it. |
| `VERGEN_RUSTC_*` | If this environment variable is set `vergen`will use the value you specify for the output rather than generating it. |
| `VERGEN_SYSINFO_*` | If this environment variable is set `vergen`will use the value you specify for the output rather than generating it. |

[§](https://docs.rs#goals)Goals

I initially wrote `vergen` (**ver**sion **gen**erator, so original) so I could embed a some git information in my
personal projects.  Now, usage has grown to the point that `vergen` needs to fit better in the rust ecosystem.

The current goals are as follows:

[§](https://docs.rs#minimize-the-tool-footprint)Minimize the tool footprint

- Adopt an opt-in, rather than opt-out strategy for the features. The default feature set is empty and no instructions will be emitted.
- The instructions you have configured **will**be emitted. If there are errors or idempotentcy has been configured, some of those instructions may be defaulted.
- Allow overriding configurtion set in `build.rs`through environment variables. This will allow package maintainers to force sane defaults when packaging rust binaries for distribution.

[§](https://docs.rs#minimize-the-compile-time-impact)Minimize the compile time impact

- I’ve removed some extraneous libraries. Any libraries added in the future will be checked against the current standard compile times to ensure the impact is not too great.
- `vergen`should compile and test from a source tarball.

[§](https://docs.rs#support-deterministic-output)Support deterministic output

Compilations run from the same source oftentimes need to generate identical binaries.  `vergen` now supports
this determinism in a few ways.

- An `idempotent`
- Recognize common environment variables that support deterministic builds (i.e. `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`
- Allow `build.rs`configuration overrides though environment variables to allow users building a binary, but not controlling the source to generate deterministic binaries.

[§](https://docs.rs#use-cases)Use Cases

I generally use vergen for the following two cases

- Generating verbose output describing a command line application.

```
~/p/r/app λ app -vv
app 0.1.0
Build Timestamp:     2021-02-23T20:14:46.558472672+00:00
rustc Version:       1.52.0-nightly
rustc Channel:       nightly
rustc Host Triple:   x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
rustc Commit SHA:    3f5aee2d5241139d808f4fdece0026603489afd1
cargo Target Triple: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
cargo Profile:       release
```
- Information endpoints in web apis

```
~/p/r/app λ curl https://some.app.com/info | jq
{
  "build_timestamp": "2021-02-19T21:32:22.932833758+00:00",
  "rustc_semver": "1.52.0-nightly",
  "rustc_channel": "nightly",
  "rustc_host_triple": "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu",
  "rustc_commit_sha": "3f5aee2d5241139d808f4fdece0026603489afd1",
  "cargo_target_triple": "x86_64-unknown-linux-musl",
  "cargo_profile": "release"
}
```

# anyhow 1.0.103 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/anyhow/^1.0.102

# Anyhow ¯\_(°ペ)_/¯

This library provides [ anyhow::Error](https://docs.rs/anyhow/1.0/anyhow/struct.Error.html), a trait object based error type
for easy idiomatic error handling in Rust applications.

```
[]
 = "1.0"
```
## Details

-
Use `Result<T, anyhow::Error>`, or equivalently`anyhow::Result<T>`, as the return type of any fallible function.Within the function, use `?`to easily propagate any error that implements the`std::error::Error``use Result;`
-
Attach context to help the person troubleshooting the error understand where things went wrong. A low-level error like "No such file or directory" can be annoying to debug without more context about what higher level step the application was in the middle of. `use ;``Error: Failed to read instrs from ./path/to/instrs.json Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)`
-
Downcasting is supported and can be by value, by shared reference, or by mutable reference as needed. `// If the error was caused by redaction, then return a // tombstone instead of the content. match root_cause.`
-
If using Rust ≥ 1.65, a backtrace is captured and printed with the error if the underlying error type does not already provide its own. In order to see backtraces, they must be enabled through the environment variables described in `std::backtrace`- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
`RUST_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only errors to have backtraces, set `RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only panics to have backtraces, set `RUST_BACKTRACE=1`and`RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=0`.

- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
-
Anyhow works with any error type that has an impl of `std::error::Error`, including ones defined in your crate. We do not bundle a`derive(Error)`macro but you can write the impls yourself or use a standalone macro like[thiserror](https://github.com/dtolnay/thiserror).`use Error;`
-
One-off error messages can be constructed using the `anyhow!`macro, which supports string interpolation and produces an`anyhow::Error`.`return Err;`A `bail!`macro is provided as a shorthand for the same early return.`bail!;`

## No-std support

In no_std mode, almost all of the same API is available and works the same way. To depend on Anyhow in no_std mode, disable our default enabled "std" feature in Cargo.toml. A global allocator is required.

```
[]
 = {  = "1.0",  = false }
```
With versions of Rust older than 1.81, no_std mode may require an additional
`.map_err(Error::msg)` when working with a non-Anyhow error type inside a
function that returns Anyhow's error type, as the trait that `?`-based error
conversions are defined by is only available in std in those old versions.

## Comparison to failure

The `anyhow::Error` type works something like `failure::Error`, but unlike
failure ours is built around the standard library's `std::error::Error` trait
rather than a separate trait `failure::Fail`. The standard library has adopted
the necessary improvements for this to be possible as part of [RFC 2504](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/blob/master/text/2504-fix-error.md).

## Comparison to thiserror

Use Anyhow if you don't care what error type your functions return, you just
want it to be easy. This is common in application code. Use [thiserror](https://github.com/dtolnay/thiserror) if you
are a library that wants to design your own dedicated error type(s) so that on
failures the caller gets exactly the information that you choose.

# bon 3.9.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bon/^3.9.3

# Overview

`bon` is a Rust crate for generating compile-time-checked builders for structs and functions. It also provides idiomatic partial application with optional and named parameters for functions and methods.

If you wonder "Why would I use builders?", see the [motivational blog post](https://bon-rs.com/blog/how-to-do-named-function-arguments-in-rust).

## Function Builder

You can turn a function with positional parameters into a function with named parameters with `#[builder]`.

```
use builder;
let greeting = greet
    .name
    .level // <- setting `level` is optional, we could omit it
    .call;
assert_eq!;
```
Any syntax for functions is supported including `async`, fallible, generic functions, `impl Trait`, etc.

Many things are customizable with additional attributes described in the [API reference](https://bon-rs.com/reference/builder), but let's see what else `bon` has to offer.

## Struct Builder

Use `#[derive(Builder)]` to generate a builder for a struct.

```
use Builder;
let user = builder
    .name
    // `level` is optional, we could omit it here
    .level
    // call setters in any order
    .is_admin
    .build;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert!;
```
## Method Builder

Associated methods require `#[bon]` on top of the impl block additionally.

### Method `new`

The method named `new` generates `builder()/build()` methods.

```
use bon;
let user = builder
    .id
    .name
    .build;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
`#[derive(Builder)]` on a struct generates builder API that is fully compatible with placing `#[builder]` on the `new()` method with a signature similar to the struct's fields (more details on the [Compatibility](https://bon-rs.com/guide/basics/compatibility#switching-between-derive-builder-and-builder-on-the-new-method) page).

### Other Methods

All other methods generate `{method_name}()/call()` methods.

```
use bon;
let greeter = Greeter ;
let greeting = greeter
    .greet
    .target
    // `prefix` is optional, omitting it is fine
    .call;
assert_eq!;
```
Methods with or without `self` are both supported.

## No Panics Possible

Builders generated by `bon`'s macros use the typestate pattern to ensure all required parameters are filled, and the same setters aren't called repeatedly to prevent unintentional overwrites. If something is wrong, a compile error will be created.

| ⭐ Don't forget to give our repo a [star on Github ⭐](https://github.com/elastio/bon)! |
|---|

## What's Next?

What you've seen above is the first page of the 📖 Guide Book. If you want to learn more, jump to the [Basics](https://bon-rs.com/guide/basics) section. And remember: knowledge is power 🐱!

Feel free to jump to code and use the `#[builder]` and `#[derive(Builder)]` once you've seen enough docs to get started.

The [🔍 API Reference](https://bon-rs.com/reference/builder) will help you navigate the attributes once you feel comfortable with the basics of `bon`. Both `#[derive(Builder)]` on structs and `#[builder]` on functions/methods have almost identical attributes API, so the documentation for them is common.

## Installation

Add `bon` to your `Cargo.toml`.

```
[]
 = "3.9"
```
You can opt out of `std` and `alloc` cargo features with `default-features = false` for `no_std` environments.

See [alternatives](https://bon-rs.com/guide/alternatives) for comparison.

## Getting Help

If you can't figure something out, consult the docs and maybe use the `🔍 Search` bar on our [docs website](https://bon-rs.com). You may also create an issue or a discussion on the [Github repository](https://github.com/elastio/bon) for help or write us a message on [Discord](https://bon-rs.com/discord).

## Socials

## Acknowledgments

[and](https://docs.rs/typed-builder)

`typed-builder`[. This crate was designed with many lessons learned from them.](https://docs.rs/derive_builder)

# cargo_metadata

Structured access to the output of `cargo metadata`. Usually used from within a `cargo-*` executable.

Also supports serialization to aid in implementing `--message-format=json`-like
output generation in `cargo-*` subcommands, since some of the types in what
`cargo --message-format=json` emits are exactly the same as the ones from `cargo metadata`.
